name: Ahornbahn
kurzbeschreibung: The Ahornbahn in Mayrhofen is Austria's largest reversible aerial tramway, carrying up to 160 passengers per cabin to the Ahorn plateau at nearly 2,000 meters altitude.
beschreibung:
Overview

The Ahornbahn in Mayrhofen in the Zillertal is a superlative aerial tramway: with room for up to 160 passengers per cabin, it features Austria's largest cable car cabins. Operating over an inclined length of 3,045 meters, the tramway overcomes an elevation difference of 1,298 meters, transporting visitors from the valley station in Mayrhofen (680 m) in just around 6.5 minutes to the Ahorn plateau (Filzenboden) at an altitude of 1,966 meters.

History & Architecture

The original Ahornbahn began operations in 1968, carrying over 11.5 million visitors across 38 operating years before being retired in August 2006. The present modern installation built by Doppelmayr (cabin design by Carvatech) opened officially on December 9, 2006. On the summit plateau, attractions include AhornSee, AhornBach, and AdlerBühne Ahorn – Europe's highest bird of prey station at roughly 2,000 meters. A special highlight is the SkyRide Ahorn, where passengers can ride on an open-air rooftop viewing deck.

Visit & Getting There

In summer, the cable car runs daily from 07:30 or 08:30 to 17:00 (departures every 15 minutes); winter season runs from mid-December to early April (as of 2025/26 season). Ascent and descent ticket: adults €40.00 (€34.00 with guest card), children €17.00, small children free; SkyRide surcharge €8.00. By car: Inntalautobahn A12, exit Wiesing/Zillertal, B169 to Mayrhofen (Ahornstraße 853, parking garage at the valley station). By public transport: ÖBB train to Jenbach, Zillertalbahn (train or bus 8330) to Mayrhofen station, then a 10–15 min walk or local bus to the valley station.

Tips

Valley and mountain stations as well as the large cabins are fully barrier-free. On the mountain plateau, the complimentary AdlerExpress shuttle provides access to AdlerBühne for visitors with reduced mobility.
